findings.title: Worker Pool Reuse Pattern is Inefficient
findings.location: Parallel Execution Strategy section, pool creation pseudocode
findings.problem: ProcessPoolExecutor is created inside the generation loop, causing pool creation/destruction overhead for each generation. Worker processes must be spawned and network data re-loaded for every generation instead of once at start.
findings.fix: Move ProcessPoolExecutor creation outside the generation loop: `with ProcessPoolExecutor(...) as pool:` then `for generation_idx in range(generations):` inside the context. This reduces overhead from ~1-2s per generation to one-time ~1-2s startup.

findings.title: Missing Loop Structure for Future Collection
findings.location: Parallel Execution Strategy section, future collection pseudocode
findings.problem: Code shows `for future in futures:` where `futures` is a dict, then uses `idx = futures[future]` - incorrect Python syntax. Cannot iterate over dict and use as dict simultaneously without .items().
findings.fix: Use `for future, idx in futures.items():` or `from concurrent.futures import as_completed` with proper iteration pattern.

findings.title: CandidateMetrics Type Mismatch with Engine Metrics
findings.problem: Design claims throughput and max_queue are returned as float by TrafficEngine.metrics(), but verification shows they are int (done=sum of ints, max_queue is int). Comments are misleading about matching engine return types.
findings.fix: Update schema comments to clarify: `throughput: float  # Coerced from int (engine returns sum)` and `max_queue: float  # Coerced from int (engine returns max stopped)`. Pydantic will auto-coerce, but comments should be accurate.

findings.title: Normalization Division by Zero Edge Case Not Handled
findings.location: Objective Function section, normalized fitness formula
findings.problem: Two inconsistent approaches shown: adding eps to denominator `/ (range + eps)` which produces large values when range≈0 (wrong), vs checking range first and setting to 0.0 (correct). First approach appears in main formula, second appears later.
findings.fix: Remove `+ eps` from division denominators. Always check range first: `if max - min < eps: return 0.0 else: return (value - min) / (max - min)`. Apply consistently for all three metrics.

findings.title: Incomplete Specification of Seed Handling for Config
findings.problem: Seed derivation uses only candidate_index: `(seed + candidate_index) % 2**32`. Since candidate_index is 0 to population_size-1 and reused each generation, Gen0 Candidate5 and Gen1 Candidate5 get identical seeds, breaking reproducibility across generations.
findings.fix: Include generation_idx in seed derivation: `config.seed = (request_seed + generation_idx * 1000 + candidate_index) % (2**32)`. Update prepare_config_for_candidate signature to accept generation_idx parameter.

findings.title: Runtime Estimation Formula is Unrealistic
findings.problem: Estimates `evals * ticks * 0.0001` implying 10,000 ticks/second, but design states 600 ticks take 0.05-0.2s (3000-12000 ticks/s). Formula doesn't account for parallelism. Will incorrectly reject valid requests or allow too-long requests.
findings.fix: Either remove runtime estimation validator entirely (recommended - rely on per-eval timeout) OR fix formula: `sequential_seconds = evals * ticks * 0.0003; estimated = sequential_seconds / min(cpu_count, population_size)`.

findings.title: Signal Timer Sorting Assumption Not Validated
findings.problem: Function sorts by signal_id assuming S1-S4, but doesn't validate that these are the actual IDs. If base_config contains different IDs (e.g., 'signal_1'), function would silently produce wrong gene ordering.
findings.fix: Add validation: `expected = {'S1','S2','S3','S4'}; actual = {t.signal_id for t in signal_plan.signal_timers}; if actual != expected: raise ValueError(f'signal_plan must contain S1-S4, got {actual}')`.

findings.title: Missing Import in evaluate_candidate Worker Function
findings.location: Parallel Execution Strategy section, evaluate_candidate function
findings.problem: _WORKER_NETWORK is used but Network import is missing from function. While object is instantiated in worker_init, type checkers (mypy) will flag undefined name.
findings.fix: Add module-level declaration: `from src.network.schemas import Network` and `_WORKER_NETWORK: Network | None = None` OR add type comment: `network = _WORKER_NETWORK  # type: ignore[name-defined]`.

findings.title: Fitness Comparison for Elite Selection Assumes Higher is Better
findings.location: Algorithm Choice section, elite extraction pseudocode
findings.problem: Fitness can be negative when penalty terms exceed throughput term. While implementation is correct (argsort + take last values), design doesn't explicitly state that negative values are handled correctly.
findings.fix: Add note to Objective Function section: 'Fitness may be negative when penalties exceed throughput. GA correctly maximizes fitness regardless of sign - higher is always better (e.g., -10 beats -20).'

findings.title: Inconsistent Variable Naming for RNG
findings.problem: Design uses `rng` throughout algorithm pseudocode but doesn't specify creation in service.py context.
findings.fix: Add to service.py pseudocode: `rng = np.random.default_rng(req.seed)` at start of run_optimization().

findings.title: Typo in Error Message
findings.location: Parallel Execution Strategy section, error handling
findings.problem: Error message uses `len(results)` which is verbose when `population_size` is available.
findings.fix: Change to: `f'Optimization failed in generation {generation_idx}: {failed_count}/{population_size} evaluations crashed'`.

findings.title: Missing __all__ Export in __init__.py
findings.problem: Design specifies empty __init__.py but best practice is explicit exports.
